title: process_dio dethrones a DODAG root on a newer-version DIO
description:
## Location

`python/src/lichen/rpl/dodag.py` `DodagState.process_dio` (root branch, ~199-202) and `_adopt_version` (~234-242).

## What goes wrong

A ROOT that hears a same-DODAG DIO whose `version` is lollipop-newer calls `_adopt_version` and returns. `_adopt_version` sets `role=UNJOINED`, `rank=INFINITE_RANK`, `_lowest_rank=INFINITE_RANK`, and copies the attacker's `rpl_instance_id` / `version`. The DIO is not used as a parent in that call, so the former root is isolated. The next same-version DIO then joins the attacker as preferred parent because MaxRankIncrease is unbounded after the reset.

Trigger (hostile mesh, two signed DIOs is enough under TOFU):
1. Root at version N, DODAG ID D, rank 256.
2. Attacker sends DIO `{dodag_id=D, version=N+1, rank=256}`.
3. Root is now UNJOINED at version N+1 with no parent.
4. Attacker sends the same version again (or any finite-rank DIO at N+1).
5. Former root installs the attacker as parent; upward traffic is captured.

`test_root_ignores_dio` only sends the current version, so this path is untested.

Rust `lichen-rpl` rejects every DIO on a root (`DodagRole::Root` → `DioOutcome::Rejected`; `adopt_version` refuses roots). C `lichen_rpl_dodag_process_dio` returns immediately when `d->role == LICHEN_RPL_ROOT`. RFC 6550 treats the root as DODAGVersionNumber authority; a neighbor advertising version+1 must not self-demote the root.

## Fix

Keep the root's "ignore DIOs" invariant: do not call `_adopt_version` from the ROOT branch. Version bumps are local to the root (or a higher-level merge policy), not a function of untrusted neighbor advertisements.
close_reason: ROOT process_dio now ignores all DIOs (matches docstring); no longer calls _adopt_version. test_root_ignores_newer_version_dio.
